sources.entry: Inquiline - Runs real Android 15 on Apple Silicon and turns each Android app into its own Mac app, with Gemini over any app, Android widgets on the desktop and per-app ad blocking. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/inquiline-app/inquiline) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Inquiline runs real Android 15 in a virtual machine on Apple Silicon Macs and presents each Android app as its own native Mac app.
summary.what_it_does: Inquiline adds Android apps to macOS: you double-click an .apk (or .xapk, .apkm, .apks) and the app appears in an Inquiline Apps folder with its own window, Dock icon, Spotlight entry and Notification Center notifications. Android 15 runs in a small QEMU virtual machine on Apple's Hypervisor framework, with graphics passed to the Mac GPU through gfxstream and MoltenVK. The README also describes per-app settings (permissions, ad blocking at four levels, widgets, storage, performance stats), a Gemini button, desktop widgets, games support with keyboard/mouse mapping and controllers, and a QR-code mode that turns a phone into a controller or touchpad over WebRTC. Google Play is not included; the README describes adding it manually with MindTheGapps.
use_cases: run Android apps on a Mac
play mobile games on a Mac with a controller
keep Android apps in the Dock and Spotlight
use a phone as a game controller for a Mac app
take screenshots or recordings of Android apps
how_to_run: Or download Inquiline-<version>-arm64.dmg from Releases, drag Inquiline to Applications, and open it (allow it once in System Settings > Privacy & Security on macOS 15+)
Open Inquiline from the menu bar and wait for Android to unpack (under a minute on first run)
Double-click an .apk file or choose Add APK… from the menu bar
Building from source: Scripts/build-app.sh --dmg (needs Xcode, Homebrew and the VM's parts, see Research/linux-gpu)
stack: Swift (macOS app, implied by Mac-native integration)
notable: Each Android app gets its own Mac window, Dock icon, Spotlight entry and Notification Center notifications rather than running in a phone-shaped frame.
Gemini can be opened over any running app and can see what the app shows, with optional Live screen sharing.
Ad blocking per app uses uBlock Origin's lists plus AdGuard's app-ads list, updated daily, and runs as a VPN and filtering proxy inside Android.
Phone-as-controller mode via a QR code and a web page on the Mac, with no install needed on the phone (same Wi-Fi required).
Free and open source under Apache License 2.0, with no account required.
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14 or later, and 8 GB of memory (16 GB recommended for big games), plus about 3 GB of disk space.
Early preview with a development build of Android that has root access; the README says not to use it for banking, payments or other sensitive accounts.

Not notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks the first launch and requires a manual allow step. Not certified by Google, so some apps that check device integrity may refuse to run; Google Play is not included and must be added manually.
